package.description: A database GUI and IDE for MongoDB, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, SQLite and Redis

en-US.description: A database GUI and IDE for MongoDB, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, SQLite and Redis
en-US.longDescription:
Monghoul is a desktop database GUI and IDE for MongoDB, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, SQLite, and Redis with Valkey, in one window with one sidebar.

- MongoDB: autocomplete from the field names and values in your collections, an aggregation builder that runs each stage, Explain that names the index a slow query needs, schema analysis, a Database Map of the references between collections, and a cluster monitor.
- PostgreSQL: completion from your schemas and joins from your foreign keys, Explain with real rows and times, and Manual commit that holds writes in one transaction.
- ClickHouse: Explain that counts the granules a read selects, and drafts with typed parameters.
- SQLite: a database file opens with no server, and every value shows exactly as SQLite stored it.
- Redis and Valkey: a key browser on SCAN, an editor for each key type, and a command console.

On every engine, edits in the result grid are reviewed before they apply, a write that can drop data or change every row asks first, and write protection, operation logs, import and export work the same way. AI assistants connect through 77 Model Context Protocol tools, and a query that reaches a database waits for your approval.

Free to use at work. Pro adds charts, the cluster monitor, document diff, custom themes and more, with one payment.
en-US.name: Monghoul
en-US.releaseNotes:
Monghoul 2.0.0

Monghoul 2.0 opens four more databases beside MongoDB: PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, SQLite, and Redis with Valkey. They share one window, one sidebar and the same tools, from write protection and operation logs to import, export and AI access, wherever the engine has what a tool reads. SQL drafts plan each statement and ask before one can lose data, and grid edits are reviewed before they apply. The first launch copies your 1.x data file and never changes it.

Highlights
• PostgreSQL: completion from your schemas and joins from your foreign keys, Explain with real rows and times, grid edits in one transaction, and Manual commit.
• ClickHouse: Explain counts the granules a read selects, drafts take {name:Type} parameters, and a mutation asks first because ClickHouse cannot undo it.
• SQLite: a database file opens with no server, and every value shows exactly as SQLite stored it.
• Redis and Valkey: a key browser on SCAN, an editor for each key type that checks your values before it writes, and a command console.
• Writes that ask first: a SQL statement that can drop data or change every row names its reasons, and Run all checks a whole script before any of it runs.
• AI tools, version 2: 77 tools with strict arguments, runs that never repeat, and approvals that hold exactly what you saw.
